newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rich German states oppose euro sanctions payments.
newsitem.headline: Rich German states oppose euro sanctions payments.

text.p: Several prosperous German states want to make sure they will not have to pay for sanctions that would be levied on countries using the single currency, the euro, that fail to keep their deficit and debts within agreed limits, a magazine reported on Sunday.

Der Spiegel said several states such as Hesse, Bavaria, Baden-Wuerttemberg and North Rhine-Westphalia want to ensure that those responsible for Germany exceeding the deficit limits after the euro is introduced would pay for the sanctions.

The magazine said that the states want the federal finance ministry to be held responsible for the sanctions. As it stands now, the states and the federal government would share the costs of the penalties, regardless of who is to blame.

Prosperous German states also support poorer states and would be required to make a greater contribution to the sanction payments. Many of the wealthier states already complain that the poorer states are not tackling the deficits with enough energy.
"We want to help, but it isn't right if those who fulfil the Maastricht criteria and reduce their debts are punished because others don't," said Hesse state finance minister Karl Starzacher.
Hesse is trying to draft legislation that would require those states whose deficits exceed their debt limits to pay a larger share of the sanctions.
